text:
leo: Thanks for the runtime deep dive today — wanted to capture a few follow-up questions that came up for my team around microbatching, KV cache behavior, and kernel ownership. Quick answers appreciated.

anya: Awesome, thanks for starting this. I'll jump in where I can and loop in owners.

samir: Happy to take the microbatching questions.

leo: First: is the microbatching change (dynamic batching based on seq length) going to be opt-in or on by default for Dedicated? I heard both at the all-hands.

samir: Plan is opt-out for Dedicated (on by default), opt-in for Private. We want to surface a compatibility flag for legacy models. Timeline: canary next week, org-wide rollout in ~3 weeks if no regressions.

miriam: For teams that rely on strict per-req latency tails, is there an expected SLO delta when dynamic microbatching is enabled?

samir: Good Q. Our measurements show p99 can increase up to ~10–15ms for small requests when batching is aggressive, but median improves. We'll provide a knob on max_latency_ms to cap batching wait.

leo: Can you share the knob defaults we plan to ship? That helps security/product decide defaults.

samir: Default we'll test with:
```yaml
batcher:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_wait_ms: 12
  max_batch_size: 128
```
Those are conservative for p95 targets; we'll tune after canary.

devon: Who owns the rollout playbook and fallback policy if we hit regressions? I can own runbooks but need the fallback mechanism implemented in the sidecar.

anya: Devon — you and Samir should pair. Samir owns the runtime change, Devon owns playbook and runbook automation. Action: Samir to open RFC w/ rollback flags by EOD tomorrow.

tess: On caching: folks asked about KV cache eviction and cross-tenant memory pressure. Will Dedicated instances share cache or is it per-tenant?

samir: KV cache is per-deployment (per-pool) for now. For Dedicated it's isolated to the customer's pool. For Hosted we have shared pools with soft-mem quotas to avoid noisy neighbors.

miriam: Is there a documented eviction strategy? LRU? TTL? Anything tunable?

samir: Current plan: segmented LRU with short TTL for prefixes > 256 tokens. Engineers can set "cache_ttl_ms" and "cache_seg_threshold" per model route. We'll post the knobs in the config docs.

leo: Great — please put sample `cache_ttl_ms` guidance (eg. conversational vs. search workloads).

samir: Will do. Example guidance: conversational -> 5m, high-recall search -> 30s, reranking -> 0 (disable).

devon: One safety ask: can we add per-customer cache memory caps so a bell can trigger before eviction cascades?

samir: Yes — adding per-customer memory cap is on the sprint. We'll expose it as `cache_max_bytes_per_customer` and an alert when >80% used.

tess: Kernel work: timeline for kernel v3 -> v4 and whether v4 will include the new flash-attention fallback?

samir: Kernel v4 targets: memory reduction, improved attention fallback for older GPUs, and a refactor to make quantization passes pluggable. Canary for v4 in ~6 weeks; depends on QA cycles.

anya: To be clear on responsibilities: Research/Applied ML to validate numeric parity, Runtime to own rollout and observability, Eng-SRE to own canary infra + alerts. I'll sync leads.

leo: Any docs or checklists we can point product/solutions teams to for customer-facing comms?

miriam: I'll draft a one-pager: impact matrix (latency/cost/compatibility) + recommended default settings. Will share by Tuesday.

devon: infra-bot: canary-deploy job for batcher-v2 -> finished 3/3 checks ✅

infra-bot: canary-deploy: batcher-v2 deployed to canary pool (pool-canary-3). All health checks passed.

leo: Thanks team. Final ask: can we have a short thread in the docs repo that lists the default knobs and the rollback steps? If yes, Samir + Devon to create PRs.

samir: I'll open the runtime RFC PR tonight and link the canary metrics.

devon: I'll open the playbook PR tomorrow morning and include runbook commands and alert thresholds.

anya: Thanks everyone — this clears up a lot. We'll track these action items in the post-all-hands doc and review next week. :thumbsup:
